english: Consider the ellipse $E:\dfrac{x^{2}}{16}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{6}=1$ and the hyperbola $H:\dfrac{x^{2}}{9}-y^{2}=1$, and let $S=(\sqrt{10},0)$. A line $L$ with slope $m$ passes through $S$, meets $E$ at the points $P$ and $Q$, and meets $H$ at two points $R$ and $T$ lying on the same branch of $H$. If $PQ=RT$, then the value of $m^{2}$ is ______.
hindi: दीर्घवृत्त $E:\dfrac{x^{2}}{16}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{6}=1$ तथा अतिपरवलय $H:\dfrac{x^{2}}{9}-y^{2}=1$ पर विचार कीजिए, और माना कि $S=(\sqrt{10},0)$ है। प्रवणता $m$ वाली एक रेखा $L$ बिन्दु $S$ से होकर जाती है, $E$ को बिन्दुओं $P$ तथा $Q$ पर काटती है, और $H$ को उसकी एक ही शाखा पर स्थित दो बिन्दुओं $R$ तथा $T$ पर काटती है। यदि $PQ=RT$ है, तो $m^{2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $E$: $c^{2}=16-6=10$; $H$: $c^{2}=9+1=10$, so $S$ is a focus of both and $PQ$, $RT$ are focal chords
Let $L$ make angle $\phi$ with the $x$-axis, $s=\sin^{2}\phi$. Focal chord of $E$: $PQ=\dfrac{2ab^{2}}{a^{2}\sin^{2}\phi+b^{2}\cos^{2}\phi}=\dfrac{48}{6+10s}$
Same branch $\Leftrightarrow 9\sin^{2}\phi>\cos^{2}\phi\Leftrightarrow 10s>1$ (then the product of the abscissae of $R,T$ is positive)
The other case $10s<1$ (chord across both branches) gives $8-80s=6+10s$, $s=\dfrac1{45}$, which is excluded
solution_full: For $E$: $a^{2}=16$, $b^{2}=6$, $c^{2}=a^{2}-b^{2}=10$. For $H$: $A^{2}=9$, $B^{2}=1$, $c^{2}=A^{2}+B^{2}=10$. So $S(\sqrt{10},0)$ is a common focus, and $PQ$, $RT$ are focal chords of $E$ and $H$ respectively.
Let $L$ make an angle $\phi$ with the positive $x$-axis and write the points of $L$ as $(\sqrt{10}+t\cos\phi,\ t\sin\phi)$.

Ellipse: substituting gives $\left(\dfrac{\cos^{2}\phi}{16}+\dfrac{\sin^{2}\phi}{6}\right)t^{2}+\dfrac{2\sqrt{10}\cos\phi}{16}t+\dfrac{10}{16}-1=0$. The difference of the roots gives the standard focal chord length $PQ=\dfrac{2ab^{2}}{a^{2}\sin^{2}\phi+b^{2}\cos^{2}\phi}=\dfrac{2\cdot4\cdot6}{16\sin^{2}\phi+6\cos^{2}\phi}$.

Hyperbola: in the same way $\left(\dfrac{\cos^{2}\phi}{9}-\sin^{2}\phi\right)t^{2}+\dfrac{2\sqrt{10}\cos\phi}{9}t+\dfrac{10}{9}-1=0$, and $RT=\dfrac{2AB^{2}}{\left|A^{2}\sin^{2}\phi-B^{2}\cos^{2}\phi\right|}=\dfrac{2\cdot3\cdot1}{|9s-(1-s)|}=\dfrac{6}{|10s-1|}$.

Branches: the product of the two values of $t$ is $\dfrac{1/9}{\cos^{2}\phi/9-\sin^{2}\phi}$. Both points lie on the right branch (on opposite sides of $S$, which is inside that branch) exactly when the coefficient $\dfrac{\cos^{2}\phi}{9}-\sin^{2}\phi$ is negative, i.e. $9\sin^{2}\phi>\cos^{2}\phi$, i.e. $10s>1$. If $10s<1$ the line meets both branches.
Case $10s<1$: $\dfrac{48}{6+10s}=\dfrac{6}{1-10s}\Rightarrow 48-480s=36+60s\Rightarrow s=\dfrac{1}{45}$. Here $R$ and $T$ lie on different branches, which the question excludes.
originality_note: New: a single line through the common focus of a confocal ellipse-hyperbola pair cuts equal chords from both, and the branch condition on the hyperbola decides between the two algebraic solutions (way 5). Closest known: length of a focal chord of an ellipse or a hyperbola inclined at a given angle. Different because: two chord-length formulas are equated and the absolute value in the hyperbola formula splits into a same-branch and a cross-branch case, only one of which is admissible.

concept_use.Chord of a Hyperbola: The chord RT of H through S has length 2AB^2/|A^2 sin^2 phi - B^2 cos^2 phi| = 6/|10s-1|, and the sign inside the modulus decides whether R and T are on the same branch.
concept_use.Chord of a Ellipse: The chord PQ of E through its focus S has length 2ab^2/(a^2 sin^2 phi + b^2 cos^2 phi) = 48/(6+10s), which is equated to RT.

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve, point and symbol is introduced, the conditions are complete, each sentence has one reading; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; it matches the Answer Plan. Checked that S is a focus of both curves, that the same-branch condition removes the second root s = 1/45, and that the answer does not depend on the sign of m. Changed: No change.
key_step: Equating the two focal chord lengths and using the same-branch condition to resolve the modulus.
justification: Two chord-length results linked through a common line, with a case split that a careless solver gets wrong. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q13 (L3), a numerical confocal ellipse-hyperbola question.
